_comment: SYNTHETIC — hand-built from the documented response shapes in Yahoo's official
Fantasy Sports API guide and from published wrapper-library samples (yfpy,
yahoo_fantasy_api). NOT a live capture. Yahoo API access is gated behind an
approval application and NO live call has ever been made from this repo.
Replace with a real redacted capture once API access is approved.
AUTHORED 2026-08-11 (not captured on any date).
MODELS: GET /fantasy/v2/league/423.l.481226/draftresults?format=json
(2023 season, game key 423 — the third season in the renewal chain)
REDACTION: all identifiers invented. Player names are real NFL players; the
numeric ids attached to them are PLAUSIBLE BUT UNVERIFIED.
WHY THIS IS COMMITTED — IT PROVES A NEGATIVE. Yahoo exposes NO per-pick
keeper flag. Not an empty one, not a zero: the key does not exist. Search
this file for 'keeper' and the only hits are in this comment. That is the
fixture's entire content claim, and it is the one a future maintainer will
doubt when they are asked 'just pull the keeper flag from Yahoo'.
The consequence encoded in parse_draft_results(): is_keeper stays NULL
because the provider did not speak. Anything we later work out ourselves
lands in keeper_inferred + keeper_inference_basis instead. A derived value
must never occupy the column that means 'the provider said so' — once those
two are mixed, no query can separate fact from inference again, and the
damage is unrecoverable rather than just wrong.
THE ANOMALY THIS FILE CARRIES — the only signal Yahoo actually gives:
picks 1-5 are sequential in pick_number but carry rounds 14, 12, 9, 16 and
11, wildly out of order, while picks 6-13 resume a normal round 1. In a
keeper league Yahoo bills a kept player to the ROUND the keeper cost, and
emits them first with the leading pick numbers. So 'round_number is
inconsistent with a 12-team serpentine' is the entire evidentiary basis any
keeper inference can have here. It is suggestive; it is not a flag; and a
league that simply drafted out of order would look identical. Write it to
keeper_inference_basis and say so.
SHAPE HAZARDS DELIBERATELY PRESENT:
1. draft_results is a numeric-key COLLECTION with a sibling 'count'.
2. num_rounds is derived as max(round_number) = 16 even though only 13
picks are present — the rounds are NOT dense, and any code that assumes
round count == picks/teams is wrong on this payload.
3. No is_keeper, no cost (this is a snake keeper league), no player_id.
TRUNCATED to 13 picks: the five keeper-billed picks plus the start of the
live draft. Reason: rounds 2-16 repeat the round-1 code path exactly.
